newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan welcomes start of pre-four way Korea talks.
newsitem.headline: Japan welcomes start of pre-four way Korea talks.

text.p: Japan on Tuesday welcomed North Korea's decision to take part in preliminary talks next month to prepare for four-way peace negotiations between the two Koreas, China and the United States.
"We have always hoped that those talks would take place at the earliest possible time, and I think this is very good," Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto told reporters.

In a meeting with U.S. and South Korean officials in New York on Monday, North Korean officials agreed to hold the preliminary talks starting August 5 to discuss procedural matters for the full session, including the earliest agreeable date, venue and agenda.
U.S. President Bill Clinton and South Korean President Kim Young-sam first proposed holding the four-way peace talks with North Korea and China in April 1996.
The aim of the talks is to replace a fragile 1950-53 Korean War armistice with a permanent peace treaty.
"This is a very important step forward," top government spokesman Seiroku Kajiyama told a news conference.
"We strongly hope that the realisation of the four-way talks will ease tensions on the Korean peninsula and that a permanent peace settlement will replace the current armistice," Kajiyama said.
